title: The Empress

seo.title: Destiny matrix 3 — The Empress: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: What arcanum 3 means in the destiny matrix: The Empress is the energy of fruitfulness and care, in its strong and weak version.
queries: destiny matrix chart calculator online 3 arcanas

meaning: The third arcanum in the destiny matrix is the energy of fruitfulness: the ability to create abundance and turn an empty place into something living and warm. The Empress does not conquer and does not invent — she grows things, and wherever she shows up life gains volume: more comfort, more people close by, more taste and beauty. To be a three is to carry a constant source inside you, one you want to give from.

In character this is a soft, slow force — not a sprint but growth. A three thinks in ripening rather than in results: finishing matters less than watching what was planted gather strength almost by itself. From the inside it feels like warmth looking for something to pour into; in an empty, cold space such a person dims, and in a beautiful, living one she opens right up.

What drives a three is the need to be a source, and its main conflict hides in the very same place. Abundance is endless only as an idea: a living person fills others exactly as much as she is filled herself. So the central question of this arcanum is how to give out of fullness rather than out of emptiness, and where the line runs between generosity and dissolving into someone else’s life.

A three shows what it is through the source it gives from. In the strong version a person first settles her own life and shares out of plenty — easily, without counting and without the quiet note of “they owe me for this”. In the weak version she gives right down to the bottom just to feel needed, and then looks for someone to blame when she has nothing left. The difference is not in how much is given, but in where it flows from — from surplus or from hunger for herself.

What sets the three apart from its neighbours in the deck is the direction of its force. The second arcanum, The High Priestess, knows and waits inside herself — a three carries that outwards and gives it a living, material shape. The fourth, The Emperor, holds the world with order and will — a three holds it with warmth and care. If the two is quiet depth and the four is firm structure, then the three between them is fruit-bearing life itself, which needs something to grow into.

article.title: 3 in the destiny matrix: The Empress, the arcanum of growth
article.short: 3 in the destiny matrix is The Empress, the arcanum of fruitfulness and growth. She changes a life not with a leap but by cultivation: she creates the conditions in which a business, a home, a family, a team or an idea gathers strength and starts to bear fruit. Two people in three have a three somewhere in their matrix (66.2%), and what it means depends on where it stands. As the calling card, it is the warmth a person brings into any conversation. In the karmic tail, it is care that quietly turns into control or self-sacrifice. Below: what the three looks like at its best and at its worst, where it falls and how often, which tails and programs come with it, and what to do with it.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 3: The Empress, karmic tails and program 3
seo.description: Destiny matrix 3 is The Empress, the arcanum of growth: where the three falls and how often, its six tails, program 3, money, love, men and women.

sections.h2: What arcanum 3 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: Three, the third arcanum, the third energy — in the destiny matrix these are all the same thing: The Empress, the third card of the Major Arcana of the Tarot. Her number is the same in every deck, so there is none of the confusion that surrounds Justice and Strength.

The card’s meaning fits into a single word, the one Arthur Waite chose for it: **fruitfulness**. Not “femininity”, and not motherhood alone, but the power to give life in general. Whatever the three touches takes on body, weight and flavour: an idea becomes a house, an acquaintance becomes a family, a small venture becomes something that feeds you. Waite called the Empress the door “by which an entrance is obtained into this life”. It is an exact clue: the three is the energy of embodiment, of the step from “planned” to “real”.

She is easiest to see next to her neighbours. [The Magician](/encyclopedia/arcanum/1) begins: out of nothing comes action. [The High Priestess](/encyclopedia/arcanum/2) knows and keeps: the idea ripens in silence. The Empress brings it out into the world and grows it. [The Emperor](/encyclopedia/arcanum/4) secures what has grown with order and protects it. Three is the first number in which two produce something new, a third; Benebell Wen calls three exactly that — “the number of creation”. How the three gets along with the four in one matrix is covered in [the combination of 3 and 4](/encyclopedia/combination/3-4), and how it lives with The High Priestess in [the combination of 2 and 3](/encyclopedia/combination/2-3).

**The three’s main tool is time.** It doesn’t push and doesn’t force. Its work is to create the conditions in which living things grow by themselves, and there are three of them: soil, tending and time. Soil is a setting you want to stay in: a home, people, beauty all around. Tending is the daily attention without which everything runs wild. Time is the patience to wait for the harvest instead of pulling up the seedling to check that it is growing. A person with a strong three thinks in seasons: what to plant now so that in two years there is something to gather.

And one more thing people often forget: she is an empress, not a servant. Her care is power over her own garden. She decides what grows in it, and she eats its fruit herself. The moment care turns into service with no say and no share, the three slides into the minus.

sections.h2: Plus and minus: the three at its best and at its worst
paragraphs: Plus and minus are not two different arcana, and not an upright and a reversed card: a calculated number never turns upside down. They are two ways of living one energy. The three’s strength and its shadow grow from a single root, the gift for growing things, so there are only two switches between them: where the person gives from, and whether they let go of what has grown.

Around a strong three, everything takes root. A new colleague feels like one of the team within a month; friends get into the habit of dropping in “for half an hour” and staying till midnight; a project someone else abandoned turns out a year later to be alive and profitable. This is a person with taste: they notice that a room feels cold and fix it in an evening — with light, food, a throw, a table moved to a better spot. Their generosity is tangible: to feed, to put up for the night, to give, to recommend.

A strong three is patient and doesn’t fuss. It knows how to invest in things that won’t pay off tomorrow: students, regular clients, relationships, a home. And it knows how to enjoy — food, warmth, beauty, the fruits of its own work — without guilt. For the three this is not a whim but a working condition: in an ugly, cold place it fades and grows things less well.

**It gives from empty.** Generosity is endless only as an idea: a living person can give only as much as they have. When the three gives in order to be loved, it soon runs into debt — of money, of time, of the heart — and starts keeping score: “I do everything for you, and you…” The difference lies not in how much is given but in the source: surplus, or a hunger for recognition.

**It cares without being asked.** Help nobody asked for becomes control: deciding for someone else, cushioning every fall in advance, redoing things its own way. A person cared for like this stops being an adult around the three, and the three resents that “nobody can manage a thing without me”.

**It won’t let go of what has grown.** To grow something means one day letting it go: children grow up, students leave, a project starts to live without its author. The three in the minus keeps what it raised close and mistakes growth for ownership: “this is mine”.

**It gets stuck in comfort.** Comfort is a condition for growth, not its goal. Once it becomes the goal, home turns into a fortress you never want to leave, and everything new looks like a threat to the familiar warmth.

**It raises other people’s crops instead of its own.** The quietest trap. For years the three tends other people’s gardens — a partner’s career, a boss’s business, the whole family’s household — and plants nothing of its own. From the outside it looks like selflessness; from the inside it feels like emptiness on the day everyone around has grown up and there is nothing left for it to harvest.

**It buys abundance instead of growing it.** A love of beautiful and delicious things with no work of one’s own behind it turns into spending: shopping as consolation, living beyond one’s means, money that is feast or famine.

sections.h2: Where the three sits in your matrix, and how often
paragraphs: A three appears in the matrix of 66.2% of people: this is a count over every date of birth from 1900 to 2026. Most often it lands in the reading by decades (28.8%) and in purpose (27.5%); least often in the material task (1.6%) and in the inner point of talent, more on which below.
You can find five of the three’s places from a date of birth in a minute. You need three numbers:

ol: **Day arcanum** — the day you were born. If it is greater than 22, add up the digits: 23 → 5, 30 → 3.
**Year arcanum** — the sum of the digits of the year. If that comes to more than 22, add again: 1985 → 23 → 5.

ul: **Born on the 3rd or the 30th** — the three is your calling card, point A (6.3%). People’s first impression of you is warmth: with you, things quickly start to feel “like home”.

**Born in March** — the three is in the spiritual task, point B (8.5%). Your gift for growing things switches on by itself, which makes it easy to undervalue. The same three opens the talent line and leads the decade from 20 to 30.

**Born in 2001 or 2010** — the three is in the material task, point C (1.6%). No other year since 1900 has given it, so the position is rare. The task is to turn care and taste into a result you can touch.
**The three numbers add up to 30** — the three is in the karmic task, point D (4.3%). Everyone with this has the karmic tail 9-12-3.
**The sum is 15 or 24** — the three is in the centre of the matrix, point E (4.6%).

paragraphs: For example, 22 March 1985: 22 + 3 + 5 = 30, so the three is in the karmic task. 3 March 1980: 3 + 3 + 18 = 24, and the three stands in the calling card, the spiritual task and the centre all at once.

A common mistake is to count 12 and 21 as threes. In the matrix, numbers up to 22 are not reduced; they have arcana of their own: 12 is [The Hanged Man](/encyclopedia/arcanum/12), 21 is [The World](/encyclopedia/arcanum/21). Digits are added up only for numbers above 22.

The other points — the family lines, money, relationships, the tail, the purposes — depend on all three numbers at once, and the matrix calculation will show them. The rarest place for the three is the inner point of talent K: from 1900 to 2026 the three landed there for people born on one single date, 1 August 2000.

sections.h2: The three in talent, work and purpose
paragraphs: The talent line in the matrix runs from the month point to the inner point K: the first number is the raw material of the gift, the second is the method, the third is what it becomes. The three most often lands here at the start, for people born in March. The raw material of such a talent is the ability to grow things. Not to invent and not to sell, but to bring to maturity: people, things, places, ventures.
Hence the work you love. The three suits work with a long cycle and living material:

ul: teaching and raising people — a school, mentoring, team development;
feeding people — a kitchen, a restaurant, farming, your own food production;
making places liveable — interiors, the home, landscaping, property;
caring and adorning — beauty, body care, clothing, textiles;
growing a product or a community whose value builds up over years.

paragraphs: What it handles badly is work done in one push: one-off projects whose result is taken away, so you never see how it goes on growing. A three who does that kind of work for years gets tired not from the load but from the fact that nothing grows.

The three stands in purpose for 27.5% of people, most often in the spiritual purpose (14.5%). Spiritual purpose describes the harmony between the personal and the social, and for the three it sounds like this: what you grow for yourself turns out to be needed by others. In the planetary purpose (7.0%), the three speaks of what will outlive you: a garden, a school, a family tradition, a venture that others will carry on.

sections.h2: The three in money and the money channel
paragraphs: The three’s money is harvest money. It comes not as one big cheque but through things that grow and stay: regular clients, referrals, repeat purchases, your own students, rent, your own production. The themes the three earns from most naturally are food, home, beauty, children and education, care, and things for the body and for comfort.

When the three stands at the entry of the money line (point L, 4.0%), a person’s first money impulse is care turned into a service. Put simply, what you already do for the people close to you, someone is ready to pay for. And in the middle of the line, at point R2, the one other people’s charts mark with a dollar sign (3.8%), the three keeps income resting on what has been grown: regular clients, repeat orders, a business that in time feeds itself.

The three’s main leak is price. The work is done well, but the bill is below the market rate, because it is “just helping out”. Cost one piece of your work in full, including the preparation, the shopping and the clearing up, and you will see how much you give away for free. The second leak is spending as consolation: a three that is short of joy buys it, and the money goes as easily as it came.

After forty (the section “How money changes after 40”, 7.8%) the three has something to lean on: what was planted earlier starts to feed you by itself. Referred clients, students, property, a name in a small circle bring in more than new leaps. The only thing in the way is the old habit of giving without counting: free advice to old acquaintances eats up the most valuable time.

sections.h2: The three in a couple and in the compatibility matrix
paragraphs: In a personal matrix, the three in relationships (12.8%) brings home, warmth and patience to the couple and expects appreciation in return. Its main imbalance is caring instead of talking: everyone is fed, everything is done, and nobody understands what the person is unhappy about. In detail — on the page [3 in relationships](/encyclopedia/position/relations/3).

If the three stands at the point under the heart, the couple is held together by care, and the risk is that care nobody asked for turns the partner into a child. This point has a page of its own — [3 under the heart](/encyclopedia/position/love_middle/3). The three in the heart chakra is a different position: it is read in the energy map, in the section on [Anahata](/encyclopedia/chakra/anahata).

The compatibility matrix is a different calculation: it is built from two dates, and its points do not mean what they mean in a personal chart. In her book on compatibility (2024), Yuliana Lisovskaya gives the three in a couple the key “fruitfulness, abundance, growth”. If the three stands where the chart shows why the couple met, the union gathers around what can be grown together: a home, a family, a joint business, a move, a household. Sometimes the task is humbler and more important: learning to handle money as a family, or thawing out after past relationships that went wrong. In the plus, such a couple looks practical and well settled, with plenty of comfort, shared projects and gifts.

In the minus, the three in a couple means rivalry over “who has put in more”, jealousy, heavy influence from relatives, money that is feast or famine, and an imbalance in which one partner grows while the other stands still and feels left behind. The author’s advice fits the meaning of the card best: each partner needs a life’s work of their own, outside the couple. The method gives no compatibility percentages.

sections.h2: 3 in the destiny matrix for men and for women
paragraphs: Gender plays no part in the calculation: a man and a woman born on the same day have the same matrix, and the three means the same thing — the ability to grow. The difference lies in how the people around them allow it to show.

**In a man**, the three makes a man of the house in the fullest sense. He builds a home, plants a garden, cooks for everyone, grows a business that feeds the family, invests in students and a team. The role of mentor, coach or owner of a small company “where everyone is family” may suit him. His taste comes from the three too: good things, good food, a beautiful place to live. A man’s shadow can be that he allows himself to show care only through money: providing, yes, but sitting down beside someone and asking how their day went is “not a man’s thing”. Then the three’s warmth goes into the wallet, and the people close to him get a breadwinner instead of a living person. The three takes nothing away from a man’s masculinity: it only shows that his strength lies in growing, not in conquering.

**In a woman**, the three is often read too narrowly: “she’ll make a good mother and housewife”. The card neither promises nor requires that: it does not predict children and does not turn motherhood into a duty. The Empress is power over her own garden, and children, home, work, creativity and a team are different beds in it — which of them to sow is the woman’s own decision. A woman’s shadow is to dissolve into the role of the one who holds everything together and not notice that she has long since stopped growing anything for herself. You can recognise it by one scene: everyone has been fed, and the hostess ate standing at the stove.

sections.h2: The three in the karmic tail: six scenarios
paragraphs: The karmic tail is the three arcana at the bottom of the matrix, read strictly in order: the entry (M), the mechanism (N) and the root (D). The three falls into the tail for 16.6% of people, and there are only six tails with it. In three it stands at the entry, in two in the middle, in one at the root. If you searched for “karmic tail 3”, your tail is one of these six:

paragraphs: All six describe the same thing — the place where the cycle of growing breaks. When the three is at the entry, the circle starts with the wish to create and fails further on: the idea is never born (3-22-19), the home becomes a cage (3-7-22), change turns into destruction (3-13-10). The tail’s entry point M is the same point where the relationship line begins, so the first reaction of such people in closeness is to look after someone. When the three is in the middle, care holds the circle together: people use it to shut out fear (18-3-12) or to entangle those close to them (9-3-21). When it is at the root (9-12-3), the task is plain: learn to take your share.

There is a shared arithmetic too: if the three stands in the middle or at the root of the tail, everyone without exception has The Lovers (6) in the centre of the matrix. Care in these scenarios is always bound up with the theme of choice and closeness.

With each generation, the three turns up in the tail more often. Among people born in 1900–1959 it is there for 14.2%, in 1960–1999 for 16.5%, and after 2000 for as many as 22.1%. The reason is arithmetic: years in the 2000s have a small year arcanum, so the sum of the date more often lands on the values that produce a three. The tails 9-3-21 and 3-7-22 occur in roughly one in twenty of this generation, while 9-12-3 and 18-3-12 have, by contrast, become rarer. All 26 tails are gathered in [the section on karmic tails](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail).

sections.h2: Program 3: the three in the karmic points
paragraphs: “Program 3” is not a separate entity. It is the name people give to a three that has landed in a karmic point of the chart. In our reading, the section “Programs: what repeats in circles” reads three positions at once: the karmic task D as the root of the repetition, the centre E as the state the repetition holds in place, and the spiritual purpose as the way out. The three stands in one of them for 23.4% of people, and its role is different in each.

ul: **In the karmic task** (4.3%), the three is the root of the scenario. Its theme is the hostess with no share of her own: the house is full, but there is no place at the table for her.

**In the centre** (4.6%), the three keeps the circle turning: the person feels good when needed, and that very feeling keeps the scenario from ending. More on the page [3 in the centre of the matrix](/encyclopedia/position/center/3). Everyone with the three in the centre has The Lovers (6) or The Devil (15) as the karmic task, and the tail [9-15-6](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-15-6) or [18-6-15](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/18-6-15).

**In the spiritual purpose** (14.5%), the three is not a trap but the way out. Whatever your circle, it is broken by the three’s own kind of action: planting something of your own, investing in slow growth, caring for yourself as well.

paragraphs: A typical three program looks like a merry-go-round: give everything — wait to be noticed — go unnoticed — take offence — give even more, so as to be noticed after all. It is easiest to break at the very first point, before your hand reaches out to help: ask whether help is wanted, and answer honestly to yourself what you expect in return. How programs work in general is explained in the article [“Programs in the destiny matrix”](/programs), and the section of the reading itself is [here](/encyclopedia/position/loops).

sections.h2: The three over time: decades of life and the year
paragraphs: The age scale of the matrix runs through the eight outer points, ten years to each. So the decade under the three can also be found from the date:

ul: born on the 3rd or the 30th — the three leads childhood, from birth to 10;
born in March — from 20 to 30;
born in 2001 or 2010 — from 40 to 50;
the three numbers of the date add up to 30 — from 60 to 70.

paragraphs: The other decades depend on the family lines, and the calculation shows them. In all, 28.8% of people have a decade under the three. It is a time of planting: what is started in these years — a family, a home, a business, a profession, a circle of people — grows for a long time and feeds you later. Such a decade carries one risk: spending it tending only other people’s gardens.

A personal year under the three is a separate subject with its own page: [3 for the year](/year/3). In short, it is a year of tending, not of leaps, and anything that ripens slowly goes well in it. If, though, by “year arcanum 3” you mean the arcanum of your birth year, that is point C from the check above — for people born in 2001 and 2010.

sections.h2: Waite’s Empress: what the classic card shows
paragraphs: On the card from the Rider–Waite deck (1909, drawn by Pamela Colman Smith), the Empress sits on cushions in the middle of flowering nature. Waite himself describes her as a stately figure in rich vestments, “as of a daughter of heaven and earth”. Almost every detail of the picture speaks of fruitfulness:

ul: **A diadem of twelve stars.** Waite himself gives the clue: among the images of the Empress he names “the woman clothed with the sun” from the Book of Revelation — the one with a crown of twelve stars on her head.
**A shield with the symbol of Venus** beside her, heart-shaped in the drawing: love, beauty, attraction.

**A sceptre surmounted by the globe of this world.** Her power is over the earthly, manifest world. Waite stresses that she is not Regina coeli, the Queen of Heaven, but the Earthly Paradise, “all that is symbolized by the visible house of man”, “the fruitful mother of thousands”.
**A field of corn ripening in front of her and a fall of water beyond** — the harvest and the water that feeds it. Behind her stands a dense forest.

**Pomegranates on her gown.** Compare the neighbouring card: the High Priestess has pomegranates on the veil behind her, while the Empress wears them on her dress. What the two keeps hidden behind a veil, the three puts on and carries out into the world.
**The cushions** she rests on, in Benebell Wen’s reading, “denote comfort”: ease here is part of the design, not a weakness.

paragraphs: Waite’s central thought about the card concerns the way in and the way out. The Empress, he writes, is “the door or gate by which an entrance is obtained into this life”, while “the way which leads out therefrom, into that which is beyond, is the secret known to the High Priestess”. He also calls her “the outer sense of the Word”: she bears the message, but “she does not herself carry its interpretation”. The three embodies; the two understands. In the system of correspondences of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, to which Waite belonged, this card is matched with the planet Venus and the letter Daleth, which in Hebrew means “door”.

For divination Waite gives the Empress a surprisingly uneven list. Upright: “Fruitfulness, action, initiative, length of days; the unknown, clandestine; also difficulty, doubt, ignorance.” Reversed: “Light, truth, the unravelling of involved matters, public rejoicings; according to another reading, vacillation.” So in Waite, the reversed Empress is no worse than the upright one. That is one more reason not to confuse the plus and minus of an arcanum in the matrix with a reversed card: in the matrix cards are never reversed; each position simply has a strong and a weak way of living one and the same arcanum.

sections.h2: What to do if you have a three

ol: **Plant something of your own.** One venture, skill or project that grows for you alone. The test is simple: in six months you can see what has grown.
**Ask before you help.** “Want help, or should I just listen?” — one question separates care from control.
**Put a price on care.** Care that has become work gets paid, even if your family is used to calling it help. Say the price out loud and don’t knock anything off for being “one of us”.
**Notice the harvest along the way.** The three discounts growth until there is a finish line. Once a month, write down what has grown stronger, even if the fruit is still a long way off.
**Let go of what has grown.** Once a season, review what you are holding on to out of habit: what already grows without you and is only waiting for you to take your hands off it.

**Your own plate first.** Your rest and pleasure are not a reward for when everything else is done but a condition without which the three grows things less well. Put them in your diary before other people’s requests.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on
paragraphs: The meaning of the card follows Arthur Waite’s The Pictorial Key to the Tarot and Benebell Wen’s Holistic Tarot (2015); the three in a couple follows Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). The points are calculated with Natalia Ladini’s method, and the shares of people are a count over all dates of birth from 1900 to 2026. The readings of the positions are our own work based on these sources. The destiny matrix is a system of self-knowledge: it describes tendencies and scenarios, but it does not predict events, does not promise children, marriage or income, and does not replace professionals.
